title: Chris Camillo / Dumb Money documented calls
policy: Every row is sourced. Personal P&L is self-reported unless a journalist is recorded as having viewed statements or screenshots. Stock-path percentages are market facts, not Camillo's verified return. Tickers that could not be confirmed are labeled. Pabst Blue Ribbon and the Vegas Golden Knights are omitted because no source links them to Camillo. This is not financial advice and is not affiliated with Camillo, Dumb Money, TickerTags, Schwager, or Business Insider.

verification_levels.independently_reviewed: Schwager statement audit and/or Business Insider review of tax forms or statements — used for career totals, not usually for a single trade's P&L.
verification_levels.screenshots_viewed_by_journalist: A journalist reported viewing purchase or position screenshots. Still not an audited closed P&L unless stated.
verification_levels.self_reported: Camillo or a close collaborator said it, in a named interview or book, without a third-party close-out.
verification_levels.self_reported_and_market_fact: The thesis and timing are self-reported; a contemporaneous market move is independently observable.
verification_levels.third_party_mention: Named by a commentator (e.g. Chart Academy, Matt Ober) without a primary Camillo P&L.
verification_levels.missed_opportunity: Camillo said he missed it, or a marketing figure is not his trade.
verification_levels.unconfirmed_ticker: A story exists; the listed vehicle is not securely identified.
verification_levels.rejected_no_source: Popular attribution with no source — not a trade in this database.

trades.name: Snapple puts
trades.thesis: A teenage Camillo noticed Snapple displacing other drinks and bought puts on a competing brand (accounts vary on the exact listed vehicle).
trades.outcome: Self-reported approximately a 3x; consistent in interviews since at least 2011. Not audited.
trades.notes: Date often given as late 1980s. Exact counterparty ticker is not independently confirmed.

trades.name: UGGs / Deckers
trades.thesis: Cultural adoption of UGG boots ahead of Street recognition.
trades.signal: Street-level and cultural observation; discussed in Laughing at Wall Street.
trades.outcome: Self-reported winning example. No audited P&L.
trades.source: Laughing at Wall Street (2011); later interviews.

trades.name: True Religion jeans
trades.thesis: Premium denim cultural wave.
trades.outcome: Self-reported winning example. No audited P&L. Marketing illustrations in the book (e.g. $1k to $750k) are unaudited.

trades.name: Nintendo Wii vs PS3/Xbox
trades.thesis: Wii's casual-gamer adoption was being underestimated versus Sony/Microsoft.
trades.signal: In-store and cultural observation. Tearsheet: a 'huge play.'
trades.outcome: Described as a large winning play. No P&L figure in the primary source we retrieved.

trades.name: Cerner electronic medical records
trades.thesis: EMR adoption wave.
trades.outcome: Self-reported 'I believe 700%' over about two years. Unaudited; wording is hedged.

trades.name: Chuggington / Facebook buzz
trades.thesis: Children's show gaining unexpected Facebook traction.
trades.outcome: Self-reported about 50% in months. Listed vehicle not securely identified.

trades.name: “Delcasse” medical-study story
trades.thesis: A medical-study related idea (some readers have guessed Dendreon; we do not).
trades.outcome: Ticker unconfirmed. Do not treat as a verified Camillo trade.

trades.name: Silicon Image HDMI — method failure
trades.thesis: HDMI adoption. Camillo later cited this as a case where personal bias overrode the method.
trades.outcome: Described as a loss and a process failure, not a model failure of the information itself.

trades.name: Target × Missoni
trades.thesis: A designer collab would sell out immediately; options around the event.
trades.signal: Pre-event consumer chatter and collab marketing. The sell-out is a documented retail event (September 2011).
trades.outcome: Self-reported doubled overnight on options, out the next morning. Event is independently documented; P&L is not audited.
trades.source: Tearsheet 2011; contemporaneous retail coverage of the Missoni sell-out.

trades.name: Michelle Obama J.Crew — missed
trades.thesis: A widely cited marketing story (sometimes '186%') is not a Camillo win. Tearsheet: he missed it.
trades.outcome: Logged as a missed opportunity, not a winning trade. Do not repeat the 186% figure as his return.
trades.source: Tearsheet 2011 (he missed it); later marketing copy that misattributes the figure.

trades.name: e.l.f. Beauty / Jeffree Star
trades.thesis: Jeffree Star and channel checks pointed to a demand spike not yet in the tape.
trades.signal: Influencer / YouTube beauty culture plus channel checks.
trades.outcome: Self-reported to Business Insider: the stock rose more than 50% in six weeks. The stock-path fact is checkable; personal P&L is self-reported.

trades.name: Restaurant Brands (Tim Hortons) — April
trades.thesis: A Tim Hortons turnaround thesis that did not play out as hoped.
trades.outcome: Part of a self-reported ~$750k loss. BI reported viewing purchase screenshots. Peak price context: $78.45 then about −59% by March 2020 (market path, not his exact P&L).

trades.name: Restaurant Brands — August add/second buy
trades.thesis: Same Tim Hortons thesis; second dated purchase.
trades.outcome: Folded into the self-reported $750k loss. Screenshots viewed.

trades.name: COVID shorts (SPY / Wynn puts)
trades.thesis: Chinese-language papers (read via Translate) implied a pandemic trajectory the US tape had not priced.
trades.signal: Primary foreign-language research, not a social-app meme.
trades.instrument: puts on SPY and Wynn; 25–30% of savings, self-reported
trades.outcome: Self-reported to Stansberry: losing at first, then 'seven figures in a week' in early March. Unaudited. He has also said he was even or slightly up in the 2008 crash after going short — separate, self-reported.
trades.source: Stansberry Investor Hour, episode 192, early February 2021 (full transcript retrieved).
trades.notes: Exact put strikes and premiums were not published. Do not invent them.

trades.name: Dorel Industries (home / bikes, COVID)
trades.thesis: Stay-at-home demand for Dorel's home and bike lines.
trades.signal: COVID consumption shift; purchase screenshots dated 24 April 2020 at $1.56, viewed by BI. Gradual selling around June near $4.46; full exit November, when the stock was $11.38.
trades.exit: gradual June ~$4.46; full exit November 2020, stock $11.38 that day (BI)
trades.outcome: The 629% figure is the stock's move from $1.56 to $11.38, not a verified personal rate of return (he sold gradually). Stansberry: '9X I think' — self-reported and hedged. Screenshots viewed.

trades.name: Peloton 2020
trades.thesis: Stay-at-home fitness hardware/software wave.
trades.outcome: Self-reported to Stansberry as maybe the biggest of his life: '$4 million… relatively small investment.' Unaudited. Entry date not precise enough for a tight event study.

trades.name: Amazon stay-at-home / later earnings options
trades.thesis: E-commerce acceleration. A later comment describes a large Amazon options position into earnings.
trades.signal: Consumption shift; later a catalyst-timed options structure.
trades.instrument: equity and, later, options (self-reported $10M options — treat as a separate, less-dated claim)
trades.outcome: Named in 2020-era interviews. The $10M options figure is self-reported in later podcasts and is not a closed audited P&L.
trades.source: Business Insider 2021; later podcasts including VladTV 2026.

trades.outcome: Named; no audited personal P&L.

trades.thesis: Coach / Tapestry cultural demand.

trades.name: Playa Hotels thesis
trades.thesis: Travel reopening / resort demand.
trades.outcome: Thesis described to BI. The stock was +32% year-to-date through 15 August 2021 — a market fact, not his verified return. Entry date unknown.

trades.name: Crocs multi-year, incl. HeyDude
trades.thesis: Crocs cultural re-acceleration, then HeyDude as a 'geographical arbitrage' (trend visible in one region before another).
trades.instrument: equity, still adding as of 2021–2022 interviews
trades.exit: still long as of Benzinga 3 August 2022
trades.outcome: In 2021 he said he was still adding after the stock had already tripled (self-reported stance; the triple is a market path). Benzinga 3 Aug 2022: HeyDude geographical arbitrage, still long. No audited closed P&L.

trades.name: GameStop January 2021
trades.thesis: He bought during the squeeze, not as a 'prediction' from YouTube titles. Stansberry: bought around $70, sold a chunk around $300–340.
trades.outcome: Self-reported on Stansberry ep. 192. Marketing that he 'predicted the squeeze' from YouTube titles alone is weaker and is not used here.
